trust_decision.summary: unarchive decides whether an attacker-supplied archive (downloaded by a scan) is safe to extract into a folder next to it. It decides this with a pre-extraction listing check (_check_archive_safe: '..' / absolute / link entries) in bbot/modules/internal/unarchive.py. The published fix does NOT change that check. It adds a post-extraction total-size cap there, plus a deny-all Unpickler for the module preload cache in bbot/core/modules.py.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Zip-Slip in unarchive, incomplete fix for CVE-2025-10284'. An engineer goes straight to the existing traversal check _check_archive_safe, which the published fix leaves untouched.

fix_sites.entry_point: unarchive internal module handle_event on a FILESYSTEM event tagged 'file' with a supported compression (e.g. produced by filedownload during `bbot -t ... -m filedownload`)
ModuleLoader.preload_cache property, read whenever the module loader preloads (any `bbot` CLI run / Preset construction); file at core.cache_dir/module_preload_cache (bbot/core/modules.py:81-82)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: bbot/core/modules.py:220-221 (pickle.load of preload cache; writer at bbot/core/modules.py:224-229)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The preload cache is a local file in bbot's own cache dir, written by bbot itself (modules.py:224-229) and unrelated to archive extraction, so a solver fixing 'Zip-Slip in unarchive' would never open it. It is also a different CWE (502), not CWE-22.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Recursive extraction of nested archives, and normal subdirectory entries (e.g. 'subdir/normal.txt') must still extract. Over-broad rejection of any '/' or of all nested archives breaks the existing tests.

O6_input_shapes: unarchive: total extracted size summed over all files after extraction, any format (zip/7z/tar/gz/bz2/xz), applied at every recursion level because extract_file is recursive (fix.diff:48-55)
preload cache: any pickled class/global reference rejected (fix.diff:14-16)

O7_producer.where: bbot/core/modules.py:224-232 (preload_cache setter / save_preload_cache writes the pickle that bbot/core/modules.py:221 loads)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: jadx module writes attacker-supplied APK/JAR contents into a folder next to the input with no bbot-side entry check (unlike unarchive's _check_archive_safe)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a decompiler, not an archive extractor. Its input types are excluded from unarchive (unarchive.py:18), and jadx sanitises entry paths itself (unverified).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file and package (bbot/modules vs bbot/modules/internal)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: re-enable a commented-out 'rar'/'lzma' 7z method, or add a gzip-only (non-tar) path, that bypasses or mis-parses _check_archive_safe's per-format listing branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The rar/lzma entries are already present but commented out (unarchive.py:24-25). The check branches on format name (unarchive.py:94), so a maintainer adding a format could easily route it to the wrong listing parser.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: download_run_artifacts extracting artifact zips with extractall/7z into the output folder without the unarchive check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Log download next to it already extracts selected zip members (github_workflows.py:197-201), so extending it to artifacts is a natural feature.

O9_family: Advisory: path traversal / link following during archive extraction (CWE-22, CWE-61). The published fix content is a decompression-size cap (resource exhaustion) plus unsafe deserialization of a cache file (CWE-502).

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 + poetry/pip. The unarchive module shells out to system 7z and GNU tar (unarchive.py:20-27, 95, 107, 110). bbot deps installer handles 7z/tar (bbot/core/helpers/depsinstaller/installer.py:37,53).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the path-component test in _check_archive_safe (unarchive.py:115-122), e.g. backslash or normalisation handling. Per the summary this is what the advisory points at, but the published fix contains no such change.

out_of_scope_notes: bbot/modules/ffuf_shortnames.py:123-127: CustomUnpickler falls back to super().find_class for any name other than MinimalWordPredictor, and loads pickles downloaded from a URL (ffuf_shortnames.py:130-145). This is a deserialization sibling of the fix's second half, but outside the zip-slip advisory scope.
bbot/core/engine.py:58-60,226,241: pickle.loads on messages over a zmq IPC socket in the temp dir (engine.py:133-134). Deserialization, outside scope.
unverified: ADVISORY/FIX MISMATCH: the advisory describes Zip-Slip (CWE-22/61) as an incomplete fix for CVE-2025-10284, but fix.diff contains no traversal or link change. The traversal/link check already exists at the pinned commit (unarchive.py:93-123) with tests (test_module_unarchive.py:244-308). Either fix_commits is mis-mapped, or the real bypass fix is in another commit not provided. Hidden tests built from this diff would score a size cap and an unpickler, not the advisory's property.

Whether the pinned _check_archive_safe is actually bypassable: e.g. how the 7z -slt 'Attributes' string looks for zip symlinks (unarchive.py:101-103 assumes it starts with 'l'), a listing-vs-extractor differential, or a backslash separator in zip entries. Not checked; no execution allowed.
jadx's own entry-path sanitisation (O8 route): not checked.
present_in_latest for O8: unknown (no latest release given).
O12: no listed red flag strictly applies. The dominant problem is the advisory/fix mismatch above, and the fix's unarchive half is resource exhaustion (0 of 7 historically).
